subject: POC onramp: hosting option recommendation, success criteria & ops commitments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medalgo.com>, Lily Chan <lily.chan@medalgo.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + POC options (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Hi Samir / Lily —

Thanks again for the demo call this morning. I wanted to capture the outcome and propose an onramp that we can move on quickly. High-level ask from your side: validate accuracy on a representative sample of clinical notes and confirm operational constraints (latency and security).

Proposed POC (4 weeks):
- Goal: show parity with current rule-based extraction on 3 priority templates and meet ops targets.
- Success criteria (you confirmed these roughly on the call):
  1) Extraction F1 >= 0.88 on the three templates measured against your labeled set
  2) 95th percentile response latency < 150ms for 1k-token queries
  3) No PHI exfiltration; audit logs enabled for all requests
  4) Clear runbook for failover and cost estimate within target range

Environment options (tradeoffs):
- Hosted Redwood API (fastest): minimal setup, quickest functional validation using synthetic/scrubbed data. Low overhead but not suitable for PHI testing.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity): predictable throughput and cost modeling; good mid-step where we can load real test sets behind controlled access. Requires contract and short lead time.
- VPC (customer-managed network): production-like, supports KMS/HSM, full audit logs and private networking. Longer setup (network + security review) but required if you need PHI in test data.

Suggested approach (recommended): short functional validation in hosted sandbox with synthetic data (1 week) followed by a VPC trial for production-like tests (weeks 2–4). This minimizes risk and gives you early signals.

Next steps I need from you:
- Confirm which environment you prefer to start with (Hosted / Dedicated sandbox / VPC)
- Share any mandatory compliance docs (SOC2 clause, KMS/HSM requirements) and a network contact for the VPC setup
- Proposed kickoff: Mon 21 Jun (we can compress if you want to start earlier)

Attachments: MedAlgo-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal + week-by-week cadence)

I'll loop in our infra lead (Olga) to scope the VPC specifics once you confirm.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medalgo.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lily Chan <lily.chan@medalgo.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + POC options (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. High level reactions and constraints from our side:
- We must keep any live PHI within our network for the POC. That means VPC or an on-prem equivalent for the production-like tests.
- For the initial functional pass, we can use de-identified samples in a hosted sandbox to validate extraction patterns, but final acceptance needs runs on our real (PHI) test set.
- Key technical questions: does Redwood support customer KMS/HSM in the VPC flow? How granular are the audit logs (per-request headers/payload metadata)? What network architecture do you need (peering vs VPN vs private link)?

Budget sensitivity: we need a rough delta between Dedicated vs Private trial to sign off quickly. If you can provide a simple TCO delta and the expected setup lead times that would help.

We can do kickoff next Monday (21 Jun) as suggested — please send a brief agenda and a calendar invite.

Attachment: MedAlgo-infra-requirements.docx (internal infra list)

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, MedAlgo Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@medalgo.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 15:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + POC options (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC)

Samir — thanks for the clear constraints. Quick technical readout and proposed ops path from my side.

Recommendation: Hybrid onramp (two-stage)
1) Week 1 — Hosted sandbox with synthetic/de-identified data
  - Purpose: rapid functional verification; narrow prompt & template engineering iterations.
  - No PHI required.
2) Weeks 2–4 — VPC trial for production-like validation
  - Purpose: run real PHI test set, latency and audit log validation, and encryption/KMS verification.
  - Requirements we will need from MedAlgo: CIDR for VPC peering, preferred auth mechanism (SAML / OIDC), KMS endpoint info if you bring your key, and a static IP allowlist for egress.

What Redwood will deliver (ops & infra owners):
- Infra: Olga Petrov will own VPC provisioning, peering, and audit/log ingestion. Deliverable: VPC onramp checklist + network diagram. ETA: 6 business days after we receive CIDR and network contact.
- Trial coordination: Marissa Cole will own schedule, data ingestion plan, and acceptance gating. Deliverable: week-by-week test plan and evaluation harness. ETA: 2 business days to share draft.
- Commercial: Ben Carter will own any Dedicated capacity quotes and contract coordination. Deliverable: Dedicated vs Private trial delta estimate. ETA: 2 business days.

Security notes:
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys in the VPC flow (bring-your-KMS or use our KMS with HSM-backed keys). We will need the KMS provisioning window for validation.
- Audit logs: per-request metadata plus full request/response hashes are available and can be pushed to your logging endpoint (SIEM) over secure channel.

Action items and owners (short):
- Samir: confirm we can use an initial synthetic set for week 1 and provide CIDR + infra contact for VPC (due: Thu 18 Jun).
- Marissa: draft week-by-week test plan and send calendar invites for kickoff (due: Fri 18 Jun EOD).
- Ben: provide Dedicated vs Private delta estimate and sample contract terms (due: Fri 18 Jun EOD).
- Olga: prepare VPC onramp checklist and network appendix (attach after CIDR received).

Attachments: vpc-onramp-checklist.pdf, network-appendix.png
